acceptanceCriteria.text: Long output in a chat terminal wraps at the pane's right edge.
Widening the window to wide screen expands the terminal grid to fill the pane's full width, and the shell wraps at the new width (screenshot before/after).
Shrinking the window's height (and width) shrinks the terminal grid with it; the input line stays visible and typeable, never below the pane's visible area.
A unit test covers refit on grow and shrink in both dimensions, and the PTY receiving the new cols and rows.

body:
## Bug
Reported by the person in the desktop app's chat terminal:
- Text in the terminal doesn't wrap at the pane's edge.
- After widening the window (wide screen), the terminal grid doesn't expand to fill the pane's full width.
- The terminal doesn't resize downward: when the window or pane gets shorter, the grid keeps its old row count, so the input line can sit below the visible area where it can't be reached or typed into.

All three point to the grid's size (cols and rows) not following the host element's size: the fit addon's resize (`xtermKit.ts` fit/ResizeObserver) isn't reaching the visible width, or the new size isn't sent to the PTY, so the shell keeps wrapping at the old column count. Check the host element's CSS (width/height, flex `min-width: 0` / `min-height: 0`, overflow on the pane; a host that can grow but never shrink would explain the downward case), whether the ResizeObserver fires on window resize, and that the resize reaches `ptyHost`.

## Do
- Reproduce: open a chat terminal, print a long line, then widen the window, then shrink its height and width.
- Fix so the grid fills the pane in both dimensions at any window size, growing and shrinking: long lines wrap at the pane edge and the input line stays visible and interactive.

## Tests
- xtermKit / terminalView unit test: host size changes (grow and shrink, width and height) refit the grid and pass the new cols/rows to the PTY resize.
title: Chat terminal doesn't follow its pane's size: no wrap, no widen, no shrink
